title: Old-project fixture corpus for format upgrades
goal: Old LMMS and Zene projects keep loading the same way, guarded by a corpus of real old project files.
acceptance: A fixture corpus under tests/data/legacy-projects/ covers at least one project per DataFile upgrade step era (LMMS 0.4, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 and Zene 0.3/0.4) and projects using DrumSynth kits, LFO/Peak controllers, VeSTige/VST effects, ZynAddSubFX, Patman and GigPlayer.
A test loads every fixture headlessly and compares a structural summary (tracks, clips, instruments, controller connections, automation) against a checked-in expectation.
A test renders a short excerpt of each fixture that uses only built-in instruments and compares it against a stored reference within a stated tolerance.
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). The DataFile upgrade chain (30 steps back to 2007) is what makes old projects load; the replacements below each convert old data on load and need this corpus to prove nothing changed.

title: Render the bundled DrumSynth kits to FLAC
goal: The bundled drum kits play from ordinary FLAC samples; the 2000-era .ds synth only runs when a user imports their own .ds file.
acceptance: The 764 bundled data/samples/drumsynth/*.ds kits are rendered once to FLAC by a reproducible script in the repository, and the rendered files ship instead of the .ds files.
Loading a project that references a bundled .ds path plays the rendered FLAC; the redirect happens in the project upgrade step and the fixture corpus proves the audio matches the old render.
The browser's background indexer never runs the DrumSynth reader; importing a user's own .ds file still works.
DrumSynth.cpp no longer uses strtok or any other non-reentrant parser state (coordinate with the queued port job new-p11-92-port-port).

Old projects that use it still load and render as before (proven with old fixture projects added to the shared corpus tests/data/legacy-projects/, which Q050-477 creates; create the folder if it does not exist yet).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). DrumSynth.cpp: 7 open findings, 13 accepted fixes, and its strtok race crashed merge train 8 via BrowserIndex.

title: Remove the OSS, sndio and libsoundio backends
goal: Zene ships only the audio and MIDI backends people use on its platforms.
acceptance: AudioOss, AudioSndio, AudioSoundIo, MidiOss, MidiSndio and MidiAlsaRaw are removed with their CMake options, build dependencies and settings entries; ALSA sequencer, JACK, ALSA, PulseAudio, PortAudio, CoreAudio/CoreMIDI and WinMM remain.

A config that names a removed backend starts on the platform default and shows one clear message saying which backend was replaced; audio.device_list and the setup dialog list only the remaining backends.
Docs, the manual and README backend lists match the build; the commands snapshot and canary figures are regenerated if any command output changes.
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). About 2.0k lines with 12 open findings; OSS is deprecated on Linux, sndio is an OpenBSD API, libsoundio has had no upstream commit since July 2023.

title: One modulation system: controllers become modulators
goal: Users and agents modulate parameters through one system: Zene's modulators.
acceptance: Loading a project with LFO or Peak controllers and controller connections converts them into equivalent modulators and targets; the fixture corpus shows the modulated parameters follow the same curves as before.
Saving writes only modulators; the controller rack window and its menu entries are removed, and everything they offered is reachable through the modulator UI.
Every controller.* command either operates on the equivalent modulator with the same result shape or is removed with its tests rewritten against modulator.*; the snapshot is regenerated live.
MIDI-learn controller mappings keep working.

Old projects that use it still load and render as before (proven with old fixture projects added to the shared corpus tests/data/legacy-projects/, which Q050-477 creates; create the folder if it does not exist yet).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). Two systems do one job: controller rack 11 open findings, modulators 32; new features must currently be built twice.

title: Host VST2 plug-ins through Carla
goal: VST2 plug-ins load through the bundled Carla host instead of LMMS's own VeSTige and Wine bridge.
acceptance: New VST2 instruments and effects are hosted by Carla (native and Wine-bridged), with editor, automation, presets and state save/load.
Projects with VeSTige instruments or VST effects convert on load to Carla instances with the same plug-in, parameters and chunk state; the fixture corpus covers it with a test plug-in.
plugin.load / plugin.list / plugin.param_* behave the same for VST2 plug-ins; the snapshot is regenerated live.
VstBase, VstEffect and Vestige are removed once nothing uses them.

Old projects that use it still load and render as before (proven with old fixture projects added to the shared corpus tests/data/legacy-projects/, which Q050-477 creates; create the folder if it does not exist yet).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). 7.2k lines of VST2 hosting on a reverse-engineered header (Steinberg stopped licensing VST2 in 2018), 13 open findings, no test files named after it.

title: ZynAddSubFX 3 instead of the bundled 2.4 engine
goal: ZynAddSubFX runs as the current upstream plug-in, not the 2.4.4 fork over RemotePlugin.
acceptance: ZynAddSubFX 3.x is hosted as a plug-in (LV2 or CLAP through the existing hosts) on every platform Zene ships, or the unit documents why a platform cannot and keeps 2.4 there.
Projects with the old ZynAddSubFX instrument convert on load with their patch state; the 962 bundled presets load in 3.x (any that do not are listed with the reason).
plugins/ZynAddSubFx and its submodule are removed once nothing uses them.

Old projects that use it still load and render as before (proven with old fixture projects added to the shared corpus tests/data/legacy-projects/, which Q050-477 creates; create the folder if it does not exist yet).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). The bundled engine is the decade-old 2.4 line and, with VST2, the last user of the RemotePlugin IPC.

title: Retire the RemotePlugin IPC
goal: Out-of-process plug-in hosting runs on one modern, real-time-safe mechanism.
acceptance: The oop.* commands (modes, crash quarantine, restart, families) run on Carla's bridges or on one new lock-free IPC layer, with their existing tests passing unchanged in intent.
RemotePlugin*, RemotePluginBase, SystemSemaphore and the shared-memory code are deleted; nothing on the audio thread waits on a semaphore or lock for an out-of-process plug-in.
A crashing out-of-process plug-in is still quarantined without taking down the app (test with a deliberately crashing plug-in).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). RemotePlugin IPC: 39 open findings in 4.7k lines, one of the densest areas in the codebase.

title: SFZ instrument
goal: Users can load SFZ instruments, the open sampler format in common use today.
acceptance: A built-in SFZ instrument (sfizz library, BSD-2-Clause) loads .sfz files with their samples, plays with velocity layers, round robins and key switches, and saves and restores its state.
The instrument is available on every shipped platform, registered in the browser and the instrument list, and reachable through plugin.load and plugin.param_* (snapshot regenerated live).
Processing is real-time safe: no allocation, locks or file I/O on the audio thread (sample streaming on a worker).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). Zene has no SFZ support at all, while it ships two legacy sampler formats (Gravis .pat and GigaStudio .gig).

title: Patman and GigPlayer become load-only
goal: New projects use SF2 or SFZ; old projects with Patman or GigPlayer still load and play.
acceptance: Patman and GigPlayer no longer appear in the new-instrument list, browser or plugin.list defaults; existing projects with them load and render as before (fixture corpus).
The instrument's window offers converting to the SFZ or SF2 instrument where an equivalent file exists, and says plainly that the format is legacy.

Old projects that use it still load and render as before (proven with old fixture projects added to the shared corpus tests/data/legacy-projects/, which Q050-477 creates; create the folder if it does not exist yet).
why: Owner-approved replacement from the 2026-10-19 hotspot report (research/reviews/hotspots-2026-10-19/report.html). Patman 5 open in 870 lines, GigPlayer 11 open and 12 fixes in 2.3k lines; formats from the 1990s and 2000s.

title: Validate and own saved plugin waveform data through one shared loader
goal: Malformed or truncated saved waveform data cannot trigger an out-of-bounds read, leak overwritten decoded buffers, or introduce nonfinite samples; valid existing presets retain identical data and audio.
acceptance: A direct loader regression and at least two affected plugin load paths demonstrate the representative short-buffer/ownership failures on the prior code; cover every migrated caller on fixed code.
Tests cover empty, invalid, truncated, excessive, misaligned and nonfinite encoded data with bounded memory use and no out-of-range access; run the affected fixtures under ASan where supported.
All migrated callers use validated lengths and owning storage; repeated loads produce no leak under the selected supported leak checker.
Representative valid saved presets load/save with identical waveform values and render equivalently under the repository audio comparison contract.
A project-level or existing control-socket fixture loads an affected instrument/effect, reloads its saved graph data, and verifies the resulting state and usable audio.
why: Watsyn, MultitapEcho and WaveShaper decode into raw allocated buffers and call a graph setter that takes no source length. This source pattern is confirmed; this assessment did not run a reproducer. Keep as a focused reliability feature. Existing drop/import/descriptor tasks share a theme but are not equivalent acceptance scope.
implementation_stages: Shared loader plus initial affected caller
approval: Owner replied 'all' to A (four additions), B1 and B2 on 2026-10-25.

title: Enforce consistent mutation, undo and modified-state bookkeeping
goal: A successful edit consistently records the correct inverse/checkpoint and modified state; a failed or no-op edit leaves project state and undo history unchanged.
acceptance: Reproduce at least one genuine missing-undo/modified-state failure and one no-op or failed-edit history failure against the pinned baseline; if no gaps remain, close the relevant stage with evidence.
A mutating command exercised through the control socket preserves before/after state across undo/redo, marks genuine edits modified, and records the documented reversible/irreversible classification.
Repeated same-value calls, typed refusals and dry runs leave state, undo history and provenance unchanged except where a documented contract explicitly permits otherwise.
Existing regression cases remain green for undone_commands spans, coalescing, nested wrappers, async mastering completion, empty inverses on first saves, and append-only provenance.
UI and headless paths use the same existing mutation mechanism; a migrated family no longer duplicates the bookkeeping that caused its reproduced failures.
why: The root-cause review links 14 transaction-payload candidate reports in 11 files, plus separate no-op and modified-flag groups. The registry already centralizes recording and documented fallback handling; residual gaps must be demonstrated before extending it. Coordinate shared helpers with scoped-agent undo and plugin gesture undo, while preserving their separate product acceptance. Do not merge all undo-themed tasks into one oversized feature.
implementation_stages: Contract audit and selection of demonstrated gaps
Additional families grouped by shared root cause
approval: Owner replied 'all' to A (four additions), B1 and B2 on 2026-10-25.

title: Use cooperative worker shutdown and explicit callback ownership
goal: Workers stop and release resources predictably, and callbacks cannot access destroyed owners, while realtime processing remains nonblocking.
acceptance: A deterministic test reproduces a concrete race, hang or stale-owner access before its corresponding stage change; repeatedly closing a worker blocked on input reaches completion within an explicit justified bound.
Resources are closed only after the worker and dependent callbacks can no longer use them; duplicate cancel/stop and partial startup failure are tested.
Race/lifetime tests execute under the applicable TSan/ASan configuration with no added suppressions hiding the reproduced path.
An allocation/locking check on affected audio-thread entry points remains clean; worker wakeup and plugin IPC changes preserve audio/MIDI delivery and existing timeout semantics.
Each supported platform changed has a real or mocked blocking-I/O shutdown regression; unavailable device/platform coverage is explicitly reported, not passed vacuously.

The implementation plan identifies surviving versus retiring worker paths, existing feature ownership and prerequisites; no competing OSS/sndio/libsoundio or RemotePlugin modernization is introduced alongside Q050-479/Q050-483.
why: Candidate groups repeat shutdown flags, forced thread termination, callback lifetime and plugin IPC ownership concerns. Current ALSA raw MIDI and OSS shutdown paths use a timed wait followed by terminate; this is a review target, not itself a reproduced failure. Coordinate with Q050-479 and Q050-483 retirement plans first; this feature owns surviving lifecycle mechanisms and necessary interim safety fixes. Other related recording, jobs, MIDI, descriptor and crash-reporting acceptance stays separately testable.
implementation_stages: Inventory surviving/retiring paths and their owners
One surviving MIDI worker with a reproduced failure
Surviving host/callback family after separate ownership design; minimal interim containment only in retiring code
approval: Owner replied 'all' to A (four additions), B1 and B2 on 2026-10-25.

title: Make session and clip state transitions preserve shared invariants
goal: Launch, stop, edit, record, undo and reload transitions leave the launcher, arrangement and project model mutually consistent.
acceptance: Stage one delivers a source-backed transition map and executable tests for representative reproduced failures; unresolved design claims are not counted as fixes.

A deterministic sequence test covers launch/stop/edit/undo/redo plus save/load, verifies stable authored identities and references, and excludes transient playback fields from persistence comparisons where the contract requires.
Control-socket tests drive at least one MIDI and one audio session workflow, including recording-to-arrangement where supported, then verify readback and rendered/audio events.
Existing quantisation, follow-action, legato, linked-content and scene behaviour remains unchanged for valid workflows.
Any introduced common transition API is used by the affected UI and agent routes and performs no allocation/locking on realtime paths.
why: Session/clip candidates are concentrated enough to merit investigation, but counts alone do not identify a shared cause or justify replacing the scheduler. Coordinate with launcher and arrangement features through shared transition prerequisites. Merge only duplicated acceptance, preserving distinct recording, mapping and editing capabilities.
implementation_stages: Reproduction, transition map and invariant tests
One common transition boundary where evidence justifies it
Expand to related edit/record workflows without absorbing unrelated feature UI
approval: Owner replied 'all' to A (four additions), B1 and B2 on 2026-10-25.

title: Open VST3 and CLAP plug-in windows on Windows and macOS
goal: A hosted VST3 or CLAP plug-in's own editor opens, resizes and closes on Windows (HWND) and macOS (NSView/Cocoa), as it already does on Linux X11.
acceptance: Vst3EditorSession and ClapHostGui select the platform window type at run time (kPlatformTypeHWND / kPlatformTypeNSView; CLAP_WINDOW_API_WIN32 / CLAP_WINDOW_API_COCOA) instead of refusing every non-X11 view (plugins/Vst3Effect/Vst3EditorSession.cpp:190, plugins/ClapEffect/ClapHostGui.cpp:65).

Open, resize (host- and plug-in-initiated), close and reopen are covered by the existing in-tree VST3 and CLAP fixtures on each platform's hosted CI job; the Linux X11 path and its tests are unchanged.
A plug-in that cannot embed is refused with a typed error naming the platform and window API, never a crash or an empty window.
Content scaling (plugin.options editor_scale) is applied on Windows and macOS where the API offers it, and documented where it does not.

docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md and docs/PLUGIN-COMPATIBILITY.md state per platform what was proved on CI and what still needs a real-machine run (the owner has a Windows laptop and a Mac mini for that check).

approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Host Audio Unit (AUv2) plug-ins on macOS
goal: macOS builds list, load, play, automate, save and restore Audio Unit v2 instruments and effects, with their own Cocoa views.
depends_on: Open VST3 and CLAP plug-in windows on Windows and macOS
acceptance: plugin.list reports an 'au' format on macOS builds only; discovery uses the system component registry and records each component in the scan cache with the same quarantine rules as VST3/CLAP.
An AU instrument plays MIDI and an AU effect processes audio through the same device/chain model; parameters are reachable through plugin.param_get/param_set and automation.
plugin.state_save/state_load and project save/reopen round-trip an AU's ClassInfo state; a component that fails to instantiate is refused with a typed error.
The editor opens in an NSView (shared with Q050-490's macOS path).

Tests run on the hosted macOS job against Apple's built-in AU components (AUBandpass, AUDistortion, DLSMusicDevice); non-Apple builds compile the format out; real-machine checks are listed for the owner's Mac mini.

approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Generic accessible parameter editor for hosted plug-ins
goal: Every hosted plug-in has a host-drawn, keyboard- and screen-reader-operable parameter view that works when its own window cannot be used.
acceptance: A 'Parameters' view lists every plug-in parameter with name, current value with units/text, range and type, searchable by name; read-only and output parameters are shown as such and cannot be edited.
Arrow keys, Page keys, Home/End and typed values change a parameter; each change is one undo step and is announced through the existing accessible announcements.
The view exposes Qt accessible name/role/value for every row and passes window.accessibility_report with no unnamed or unreachable control.
Presets/programs exposed by the plug-in are listed and selectable from the same view.
Works for VST3, CLAP and LV2 devices; a control-socket test drives the view on the in-tree fixtures.
why: The accessibility research ranked inaccessible third-party plug-in windows the biggest barrier for blind producers; the same view is the fallback when an editor fails to embed.
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Warp controls for launcher audio cells in the GUI
goal: An audio cell's gain, transpose, detune, loop region and tempo-warp settings are editable from the launcher GUI, not only over the socket.
acceptance: The launcher cell's context menu or inspector exposes every warp/playback field that session.set_slot accepts (docs/050-features/Q050-013.md:29-35 lists them as socket-only).
Edits are undoable, saved and reloaded, and reflected in the cell's display.
A GUI test drives each control and verifies the cell's state through session.get_state; rendered audio changes as the existing Q050-013 PCM tests expect.
The KNOWN-LIMITATIONS socket-only note for these fields is removed.

approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: A GUI switch for sample-accurate automation curves
goal: Users can see and change whether an automation clip renders sample-accurately from the automation editor.
acceptance: The automation editor shows the clip's sample-accuracy mode and lets the user change it; the change is undoable and saved.
The control uses the same path as automation.ramp_set / automation.ramp_get and agrees with them.
A GUI test toggles the mode and verifies it through automation.ramp_get; docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md:2169-2210 is updated.

title: Extract a video's audio from the GUI
goal: The video window offers an 'Extract audio' action that places the attached video's sound on an audio track.
acceptance: A menu action in the video window or video lane runs video.extract_audio in its background mode and shows progress in the task area.
The extracted audio lands on a new audio track aligned to the video's offset; the action is undoable.
A GUI test runs the action on the in-tree test video fixture; builds without FFmpeg hide the action.
why: The manual promises extraction but no GUI caller exists (DAW coverage audit).
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Noise reduction as a sample-editor range operation
goal: Users can reduce steady background noise in a selected range of a sample from the sample editor.
acceptance: sample.edit_range gains a denoise operation that processes the selected range offline with the existing RNNoise denoiser (plugins/RnnoiseDenoiser), resampling as that plug-in does.
The Sample Editor exposes it with an amount control and preview; the edit is undoable like the other range operations.
A test on a fixture with added noise shows a measured noise-floor drop and an unchanged length; non-speech material is documented as out of scope for RNNoise.
why: Podcast and voice workflows lack a repair step (DAW coverage audit); the RNNoise effect exists only as a mixer insert.
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Earcons for focus, edit and transport feedback
goal: Short, optional sounds confirm common actions so screen-reader users do not have to wait for speech.
acceptance: A small earcon set (selection boundary, edit applied, refused action, record start/stop, loop wrap) plays through a monitoring path that is never recorded or rendered.
Earcons are off by default, switchable per category, with their own level, from the accessibility settings and over the socket.
Playing an earcon allocates and locks nothing on the audio thread (pre-loaded buffers).
A test proves earcons do not appear in render.render output or recorded takes.
why: The accessibility research found no earcon route (rg 'earcon' returned nothing).
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Switch-access scanning and dwell activation
goal: Musicians who use one or two switches, or dwell-clicking with eye-gaze or head pointers, can reach and operate the main controls.
acceptance: An optional scanning mode steps focus through the active panel's controls on a timer or a 'next' switch, and activates on a 'select' switch; switch keys are configurable.
An optional dwell mode activates the control under the pointer after a configurable delay, with a visible progress ring.
Scanning order follows the existing accessible focus order; both modes are tested on the transport, track list, mixer strip and note editor.
Both modes are off by default and documented in the manual's accessibility section.
why: No switch, eye-gaze or dwell path exists (accessibility research, section 5).
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Visual cues for deaf and hard-of-hearing users
goal: Timing and level events that are normally heard can also be seen.
acceptance: A visual metronome (beat flash with accent on the downbeat) follows the transport and count-in.
Optional on-screen flashes mark clipping, recording start/stop and launcher quantise points.
All cues respect the reduced-motion setting and the accessible palette; each is switchable and saved in settings.
Tests check that the cues follow transport position and tempo changes.
why: Deaf/HoH musicians rely on visual and vibrating timing cues (accessibility research, section 4); only haptics was ruled out.
approval: Owner replied 'go ahead and add them' on 2026-10-27 (gaps from research/strategy-2026-10-27 and the plug-in stress run).

title: Tell users when a newer Zene version is available
goal: Zene can tell a user, with their consent, that a newer release exists and take them to its download page; nothing is downloaded or installed without the user.
acceptance: First run asks once whether to check for updates (default off until answered); the choice is in Settings and over the socket (app.update_check_get / app.update_check_set), and is saved.

When enabled, at most once a day and on demand (Help > Check for updates) Zene reads the latest release of the configured feed (default: the KRUZZZZY/zene-studio GitHub releases API), compares versions semantically (pre-releases only when the user opted into them), and shows a non-modal notice with the version, release notes and a button that opens the download page.

Offline, rate-limited, malformed or slow responses never block the interface or start-up (background request, bounded timeout) and produce at most one quiet log line; no request is ever made while the setting is off.

Builds that are updated by something else (distro packages, Flatpak, a build-time option) hide the feature; the request carries no identifying data beyond a User-Agent naming the version and platform.
Tests use a loopback HTTP fixture only (never a real network): newer/equal/older/pre-release/malformed/timeout responses and the off state making zero requests.
The manual's Help section and docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md describe exactly what is sent and that installation stays manual; automatic download/installation is a later unit that needs signed installers.
why: The owner is about to send builds to testers; without a check they will not learn about new builds. ControlCommandsAssistant.cpp:32 states 'There is no update check: nothing is fetched'.
approval: Owner: 'Go ahead and make a feature for it' (update check), 2026-10-27.

title: Open plug-in windows on Wayland desktops
goal: A hosted plug-in's own window opens on a Linux Wayland session (KDE, GNOME), not only under X11.
acceptance: Measure first: on a Wayland session, report what plugin.editor_open does today for a VST3 and a CLAP fixture (PluginNativeEditor passes view->winId() as an X11 window id at src/gui/PluginNativeEditor.cpp:244; on the wayland Qt platform that is not an X11 window).

Make it work: either run the application on XWayland when plug-in editors are needed (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb chosen at start-up unless the user overrides it, as other Linux DAWs do), or host each editor in an XWayland-backed window; the choice and its reasons are documented.
When an editor still cannot open (no XWayland, a plug-in without X11 support), the refusal is typed and names the reason - never a crash, a hang or an empty window.
A test covers the platform decision (wayland session with and without XWayland available, user override) without needing a compositor; the X11 path and its tests are unchanged.
The manual and docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md state the Wayland behaviour; the owner checks it on the real KDE Wayland desktop.
why: Most current Linux desktops default to Wayland, including the owner's KDE; the editor host is X11-only (Vst3EditorSession.cpp:190, ClapHostGui.cpp:65) and nothing selects XWayland.
approval: Orchestrator-raised 2026-10-27 while answering the owner's plug-in window question; same approval as the 2026-10-27 additions ('go ahead and add them').

title: Ship .deb packages for x86_64 and arm64 (Chromebook-friendly Linux install)
goal: A Linux user - including a ChromeOS user with Linux turned on - installs Zene by double-clicking a .deb, on both x86_64 and arm64, and it appears in the launcher.
acceptance: build.yml's linux-x86_64 and linux-arm64 jobs also produce zene_<version>_amd64.deb and zene_<version>_arm64.deb (CPack DEB or an equivalent recipe), uploaded on tags exactly like the AppImage (the tag/dispatch-only upload rule in build.yml is kept).

The .deb declares its runtime dependencies (Qt, libsndfile, the audio backends) so apt resolves them on Debian 12 (ChromeOS Crostini's base) and Ubuntu 24.04; installs a .desktop file, icon and MIME type for .mmp/.mmpz so it shows in the launcher and opens projects.
Installing and removing it leaves no files behind outside the package's own list (dpkg -L / dpkg -r checked in CI on a clean container).
Smoke test in CI on each arch: install the .deb in a clean Debian 12 container, run zene --version and a headless render of a bundled demo project under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen.

docs: the download page / README says which file to pick (Intel/AMD vs ARM Chromebook) and the one-time 'turn on Linux' step on ChromeOS, plus the honest limits (higher latency, USB audio interfaces usually unavailable in Crostini).
why: Owner 2026-10-28: 'the most accessible possible DAW'. On ChromeOS a .deb double-clicked in Files installs into the Linux container and lands in the launcher - easier than an AppImage; many cheap Chromebooks are ARM, and CI already builds linux-arm64.

title: Composer view: optional classical notation in the note editor (off by default)
goal: A classically trained musician can switch on a composer view that shows a grand staff, clefs and note names beside the note editor's rows, while everyone else keeps a clean piano-key column by default.
acceptance: Settings has a 'Composer view (classical notation)' option in the note-editor section, OFF by default; it is saved in the config, survives restart, and is readable/settable through the existing settings.get/settings.set control commands.

OFF (default): the note editor's left key column shows plain piano keys with only the C of each octave labelled (C3, C4, ...); per-row note names, staff and clefs are not drawn. Custom drum/key names from TrackKeyNames still show.

ON: the left column widens and draws a grand staff (treble and bass clef) aligned to the piano-roll rows: each visible row's pitch sits as a notehead on its correct line or space, with ledger lines above/below and middle C between the staves; every row is labelled in scientific pitch (C4, F#3).
ON: accidentals follow the editor's current scale/key (flats in flat keys, sharps otherwise) and the key signature is drawn after the clefs; with no scale set it uses sharps.

Toggling the setting updates an open note editor immediately, without reopening it; row heights, scrolling, zoom, auditioning a key by clicking it, and accessible-mode sizes keep working in both modes.

Unit tests: the pitch -> staff position / ledger-line / accidental mapping (incl. middle C, both clefs, a flat key and a sharp key), the setting's default is OFF, and the key column paints the staff only when ON (offscreen widget test). The test fails if the default is flipped to ON.
README/user docs mention the option in one or two plain sentences.
